# ACR drift report — RiverCity Metro Rider Portal

**Prior:** `rcm-2026q3`, product version 2026.3, issued 2026-07-28 (report version 1)
**Current:** `rcm-2027q1`, product version 2027.1, issued 2027-02-19 (report version 2)
**Evaluator both cycles:** Meridian Digital Accessibility (Dana Okafor)
**Conformance target both cycles:** WCAG 2.2 Level AA, web component, catalog `2.5-edition-wcag-2.2-508-en`

## What this report is, and is not

This is a comparison of two finished, delivered documents plus the current
cycle's own fingerprint re-check table. Nothing was tested for this request.
Where this report says a defect was fixed or is still present, that is the
current evaluation's evidence as delivered, restated — not independent
verification. The comparison itself (row-level diff, sample attribution,
counts) is mine and is checkable against the two documents above.

Both documents are this engagement's own output, carrying this engagement's
`finding_id` and `fingerprint` values. No third-party document is involved,
so the fingerprints are directly comparable across cycles — which is the only
reason a row-level drift report is possible at all.

## Headline

Four things moved, and they do not all mean the same kind of thing:

1. **Three defects were fixed and closed**, including the only CRITICAL the
   portal carried. All three were verified on samples and processes that
   carried over from the prior cycle, so all three are clean like-for-like
   improvements.
2. **One defect got substantially worse** — the legacy skip-link failure
   (`5f77ab02`) spread from 2 samples to 6, took two previously-passing
   carried-over templates with it, dropped 2.4.1 from partially-supports to
   does-not-support, and was raised MINOR → MAJOR. This is a genuine
   regression on carried-over ground.
3. **One defect shrank but did not close** — the missing autocomplete tokens
   (`44b09ce6`) were fixed in checkout and not in the paratransit form,
   moving 1.3.5 from does-not-support to partially-supports at unchanged
   MAJOR severity.
4. **One new MAJOR appeared on a template that did not exist last cycle** —
   `3d90c7e1` on S14 station detail. 2.4.11 moved supports → partially-supports,
   but this is *not* a regression: it is newly-in-scope surface.

Net conformance counts improved slightly. The net counts are the least
informative thing in this comparison — see "Why the net counts mislead" below.

## 1. Document metadata drift

| Field | rcm-2026q3 | rcm-2027q1 | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `product.version` | 2026.3 | 2027.1 | New major release |
| `report_date` | 2026-07-28 | 2027-02-19 | |
| `version` | 1 | 2 | Report revision, not product version |
| `evaluation_methods_used` | WCAG-EM 2.0; 11 structured + 1 random + 2 complete processes | Same counts, plus "re-evaluation" and the carry-over declaration | The carry-over declaration is new and is the right addition |
| `title`, `author`, `legal_disclaimer`, `notes`, `catalog` | — | — | Byte-identical |
| All four disabled chapters | — | — | Byte-identical notes |
| AAA chapter | empty, "not evaluated at target" | empty, same note | Unchanged |

The disabled chapters (functional performance criteria, hardware, software,
support documentation) carry identical boundary notes in both cycles. **No
drift can be reported for the RideRC native app or the PDF timetables** —
those surfaces are outside both documents' evaluation method, and the
identical notes are a documentation fact, not evidence that nothing changed
there.

## 2. Sample-frame drift — read this before reading the row table

The sample changed materially between cycles. Any level change can come from
the product changing, the sample changing, or both, and the two documents do
not separate those on their own.

| | Samples |
|---|---|
| **Carried over (7 structured + both processes)** | S01 home, S02 trip planner, S03 route schedule, S06 account dashboard, S07 checkout, S08 contact + paratransit form, S11 title-vi; P01 (web, both branches), P02 (non-web) |
| **Retired (4 structured + 1 random)** | S04 service alerts, S05 fares, S09 news article, S10 accessibility policy, R01 /riders/lost-and-found |
| **Added (4 structured + 1 random)** | S12 alerts subscription (shipped 2026-11), S13 fare calculator (rebuilt 2026-10), S14 station detail (shipped 2026-12), S15 news index, R02 /riders/bike-racks |

Two retirements are described as replacements: S13 replaces the 2026 fares
page (S05) and S15 replaces the 2026 news article template (S09). **S04
service alerts and S10 accessibility policy were retired with no stated
replacement.** S12 "alerts subscription" is a new template, not described as
the successor to S04.

Random sample: R01 (seeded shuffle of a 214-URL sitemap, seed 7391) → R02
(251-URL sitemap, seed 8815). The site grew about 17% by URL count while the
structured sample stayed at 11, so sampled coverage fell from 12/214 (5.6%) to
12/251 (4.8%). WCAG-EM's structured sample is not proportional, so this is not
a method defect — it is a comparability caveat worth stating in the published
report.

Accessibility support baseline is identical across both cycles (NVDA 2026.1 +
Firefox 141; VoiceOver + Safari 18; TalkBack 15 + Chrome; keyboard-only). That
is what makes the carried-over comparisons trustworthy — nothing in the AT
stack moved underneath them.

## 3. Conformance drift, row by row

56 A/AA rows in both documents (32 Level A, 24 Level AA). No rows were added
or removed. **49 rows are byte-identical.** Seven rows differ:

| SC | Prior | Current | Direction | Finding | Comparison basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2.1.1 Keyboard | partially-supports | **supports** | Fixed | `a11y_fare_zone_slider_keyboard` (7c1f22ab) closed | Like-for-like — S07 and P01 both carried over |
| 3.3.1 Error Identification | partially-supports | **supports** | Fixed | `a11y_payment_error_association` (c30e51f9) closed | Like-for-like — P01 declined-payment branch carried over |
| 4.1.3 Status Messages | partially-supports | **supports** | Fixed | `a11y_purchase_confirm_silent` (e8c2447d) closed | Like-for-like — P01 default branch carried over |
| 1.3.5 Identify Input Purpose | does-not-support | **partially-supports** | Improved, not closed | `a11y_form_autocomplete_missing` (44b09ce6) still open | Like-for-like — S07 fixed, S08 not; both carried over |
| 2.4.1 Bypass Blocks | partially-supports | **does-not-support** | **Regressed (two levels)** | `a11y_legacy_skiplink_anchor` (5f77ab02), MINOR → MAJOR | Like-for-like — S03 and S06 carried over and previously passed |
| 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured | supports | **partially-supports** | New defect, not a regression | `a11y_sticky_filterbar_obscures_focus` (3d90c7e1), new MAJOR | **Not comparable** — S14 has no prior-cycle counterpart |
| 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum) | partially-supports | partially-supports | **Level unchanged**; citation changed S03+S09 → S03+S15 | `a11y_route_badge_contrast` (2ab9d871) unchanged, MAJOR, 2.8:1 vs 4.5:1 | Like-for-like on S03; the S09→S15 swap is sample churn, not movement |

4.1.2 (`a11y_swap_button_name`, 91d4e0c3) is unchanged in level, note text,
scope, and severity — the one open finding that is genuinely static.

### The regression, in detail

2.4.1 is the only row that got worse, and it deserves the space. The legacy
info-page shell was rolled out across the schedules and account areas in
2026-11. In the prior cycle the missing skip-link target failed in R01 and S11
only. It now fails in S03, S06, S11, S12, S15 and R02. Of those, **S03 route
schedule and S06 account dashboard carried over from the prior sample and
passed 2.4.1 there.** That subset alone establishes the regression without
any reliance on the new samples — a shipped platform change broke two
templates that previously conformed, and the same shell was used to build
three of the new templates. The evaluator raised the severity MINOR → MAJOR
accordingly.

This is the item where the direction of travel matters most: the fixes closed
defects on specific components, while this one propagated through a shared
shell. Component-level and shell-level defects have different blast radii and
different fix economics, and the current sample very likely understates the
shell's footprint (see section 6).

## 4. Findings ledger drift

Prior cycle carried 7 open findings. Current cycle carries 5.

| finding_id | fingerprint | Prior | Current | Severity |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `a11y_fare_zone_slider_keyboard` | 7c1f22ab | Open (2.1.1) | **Closed** | was CRITICAL |
| `a11y_payment_error_association` | c30e51f9 | Open (3.3.1) | **Closed** | was MAJOR |
| `a11y_purchase_confirm_silent` | e8c2447d | Open (4.1.3) | **Closed** | was MAJOR |
| `a11y_legacy_skiplink_anchor` | 5f77ab02 | Open (2.4.1) | Open, wider | MINOR → **MAJOR** |
| `a11y_form_autocomplete_missing` | 44b09ce6 | Open (1.3.5) | Open, narrower | MAJOR (unchanged) |
| `a11y_route_badge_contrast` | 2ab9d871 | Open (1.4.3) | Open, same | MAJOR (unchanged) |
| `a11y_swap_button_name` | 91d4e0c3 | Open (4.1.2) | Open, same | MINOR (unchanged) |
| `a11y_sticky_filterbar_obscures_focus` | 3d90c7e1 | — | **New** (2.4.11) | MAJOR |

Open severity mix: **CRITICAL 1 → 0. MAJOR 4 → 4. MINOR 2 → 1.**

The flat MAJOR count hides complete turnover in composition: two MAJORs
closed, one MINOR raised into the tier, one new MAJOR added.

All four carried findings kept their `finding_id` and `fingerprint` across
cycles. That stability is what makes this report possible; preserve it.

## 5. Why the net counts mislead

| Adherence level | rcm-2026q3 | rcm-2027q1 |
|---|---|---|
| supports | 40 | 42 |
| partially-supports | 6 | 4 |
| does-not-support | 1 | 1 |
| not-applicable | 9 | 9 |
| **Total A + AA** | **56** | **56** |

Read alone, this says "modest improvement, worst tier unchanged." Both halves
of that reading are wrong:

- **"Worst tier unchanged" is backwards.** The does-not-support count is 1 in
  both cycles because 1.3.5 left the tier (partial fix) and 2.4.1 entered it
  (regression). Different row, different direction, same count.
- **"+2 supports" undercounts the good news and hides the bad.** Three defects
  actually closed; only two of those show up as a supports gain, because the
  third (1.3.5) improved without closing. Meanwhile 2.4.11's move out of
  supports is not a loss of ground at all — it is new ground being measured
  for the first time.

Counts of adherence levels track the sample's footprint. They do not track
user impact, and in a cycle with 36% sample turnover they do not track
progress either. Report the ledger in section 4, not this table.

## 6. Three specific misreadings to avoid

**Do not read 2.4.11 as a regression.** S14 station detail shipped 2026-12 and
has no counterpart in the rcm-2026q3 sample. The prior "supports" was a claim
about the prior sample, which did not contain this template. Nothing that
previously passed now fails. Correct framing: a new template shipped with a
new MAJOR defect.

**Do not read 1.4.3's citation change as movement.** "S03 and S09" → "S03 and
S15" looks like one page fixed and another broken. Neither happened. S09 was
retired, S15 replaced it, and both render the same route-badge component at
the same measured 2.8:1. The finding did not move; the sample did. If
anything the swap strengthens the finding: the defect follows the component,
not the page, so its real footprint is wider than either citation list.

**Do not read any "supports" row as covering the retired samples.** S04
service alerts and S10 accessibility policy left the sample without stated
replacements. Given that the legacy shell rollout broke 2.4.1 on every
carried-over template built on it, whether S04 and S10 are now on that shell
is an open and material question — and this ACR cannot answer it.

## 7. What these two documents do not establish

- **Conformance of retired surfaces.** S04, S05 (as it existed), S09, S10 and
  the R01 URL are not covered by the current cycle. S05 and S09 have stated
  successors; S04 and S10 do not.
- **The true footprint of the legacy-shell defect.** The current sample shows
  6 of 12 sampled surfaces failing. The shell was rolled out "across the
  schedules and account areas"; how many unsampled URLs it reaches is not
  measured. Same caveat, smaller, for the route-badge component.
- **Whether the new templates carry input-purpose fields.** The prior cycle's
  1.3.5 note scoped itself explicitly ("every sample where input-purpose
  fields exist"); the current note does not restate that scoping for S12–S15.
- **Anything about non-web surfaces.** The native app and PDF timetables sit
  outside both documents' evaluation method. Their disabled-chapter notes are
  unchanged, which says nothing about whether those surfaces changed.
- **Independent confirmation of the three closures.** The re-check table is
  the current evaluation's own evidence. This report restates it; it does not
  corroborate it.

## 8. Accuracy issues in the delivered rcm-2027q1 document

Two wording items to correct before the Authority publishes. Neither changes
any conformance conclusion.

1. **2.4.1's note overstates the footprint.** It reads "the majority of the
   sample." The current sample is 11 structured + 1 random = 12; the note
   lists 6 failures (S03, S06, S11, S12, S15, R02). Six of twelve is half, not
   a majority. Suggested correction: "half the sample (6 of 12)." The failure
   list itself is consistent with the re-check table; only the characterization
   is wrong. In a document relied on for procurement, an overstatement in the
   evaluator's favor of accuracy is still an overstatement.

2. **`evaluation_methods_used` names only P01 as carried over**, while the
   engagement record carries both complete processes forward. This is
   defensible in a web-component ACR — P02 is the non-web native-app process —
   but a reader holding both documents will notice the mismatch. Consider
   "both complete processes (P01 web; P02 non-web, outside this component)."

---

# Handoff note — engagement owner

**Subject:** rcm-2026q3 → rcm-2027q1 drift report, ready with three items needing your call

The drift comparison is done and above. It is a document-to-document
comparison plus the current cycle's re-check table; no new testing was
performed and none was requested.

**The story to tell the Authority.** The portal fixed three defects including
its only CRITICAL, and all three closures sit on samples and processes that
carried over from 2026.3 — so they are real, not sampling artifacts. Against
that, a platform change made in 2026-11 broke bypass-blocks on templates that
previously conformed, which is now the portal's most consequential open item.
Net adherence counts barely moved and should not lead the narrative; the
findings ledger should.

**Three items that need a decision before this leaves the building.**

1. **Fix the "majority of the sample" wording in 2.4.1.** Six of twelve is
   half. It is a small error in a document that gets read by procurement
   officers, and it is the kind of thing that costs an evaluator credibility
   disproportionately. Section 8 has the suggested replacement.

2. **Decide what to say about S04 and S10.** Service alerts and accessibility
   policy left the sample with no stated successors, in the same cycle that a
   shared shell broke bypass-blocks everywhere it landed. I would state the
   gap explicitly in the transmittal rather than let a reader infer coverage
   that does not exist. If the Authority wants those two surfaces covered,
   that is a scope conversation, not a correction.

3. **Confirm the disclaimer is intentional.** Both reports carry "Draft for
   review — not a legally binding conformance claim until reviewed and issued
   by RiverCity Metro Authority," and the Authority publishes an ACR per major
   release. If the 2026.3 report was published with that line intact, someone
   should know that before the 2027.1 one follows it. I have no visibility
   into what was actually published — this is a question, not a finding.

**What to protect in the next cycle.** The four carried findings kept their
`finding_id` and `fingerprint` values across both cycles. That is the only
reason this comparison could be made at the row level instead of by reading
prose side by side. Keep the identifiers stable, and keep declaring the
carry-over set in `evaluation_methods_used` the way rcm-2027q1 does — with 36%
sample turnover, that declaration is what separates a real comparison from a
guess.

**One thing I would watch.** The legacy shell and the route-badge component
are both defects that travel with a shared artifact rather than living on a
page. The sample shows where they were caught, not where they are. If the
Authority asks "how many pages are affected," the honest answer is that the
sample cannot say — and the useful answer is a code-level inventory of where
the shell and the badge component are used, which is cheaper than expanding
the sample and gives a definite number.

**Confidence.** High on the row-level diff, the counts, and the arithmetic —
all of it is checkable against the two documents. High on the attribution of
each change to carried-over versus new samples. Dependent on the delivered
evidence for the three closures and the severity ratings; I did not re-verify
those and this report should not be read as corroborating them.

— Prepared from the rcm-2026q3 and rcm-2027q1 ACRs as delivered, and the
rcm-2027q1 fingerprint re-check table.
